NAME: Comprehensive review of AI-driven multiscale modeling approaches for solid‑state physics and chemistry
TYPE: method

DIRECT_CLAIMS: Artificial intelligence has transformed multiscale modeling by linking atomic, mesoscale, and continuum scales, delivering improved accuracy and reduced computational cost compared with traditional methods.

DIRECT_CLAIMS: Machine‑learning‑driven interatomic potentials (e.g., GAP, DeePMD) and DFT‑trained surrogate models enable simulations of up to millions of atoms while retaining accuracy close to first‑principles benchmarks, making large‑scale high‑fidelity simulations feasible.

DIRECT_CLAIMS: Neural‑network‑based electronic‑structure prediction tools achieve significant speedups over conventional density‑functional theory while maintaining comparable accuracy, accelerating electronic‑structure calculations.

DIRECT_CLAIMS: Graph neural network architectures such as MEGNet and SchNet enhance prediction of phase transitions, defect dynamics, and bulk material properties relative to classical computational approaches.
ARTICLE: Artificial Intelligence for Multiscale Modeling in Solid-State Physics and Chemistry: A Comprehensive Review

NAME: Universal MLIPs
TYPE: method
DIRECT_CLAIMS: Universal MLIPs trained on massive datasets can generalize across diverse chemical systems and can be successfully applied to structural optimization and lattice dynamics workflows.
DIRECT_CLAIMS: Each cataloged DFT structure provides one energy and 3N forces (N = number of atoms) for training universal MLIPs.
DIRECT_CLAIMS: Universal MLIPs attempt to cover 10-100 elements under varying levels of constraints.
DIRECT_CLAIMS: Orb-v3-direct-* models are the only universal MLIPs that can compute hundreds of forward passes per second, exceeding one million steps per hour for small systems.
ARTICLE: Pushing the limits of unconstrained machine-learned interatomic potentials

NAME: PET
TYPE: cited_work

DIRECT_CLAIMS: The PET model achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on matbench-discovery benchmark (DAF=6.075, Accuracy=0.977, F1=0.924) and exceeds SOTA on SPICE molecular benchmark across most subsets for both energy and force predictions.

DIRECT_CLAIMS: PET-OMAD demonstrates the best overall accuracy in predicting energies and forces on MADBench in almost all cases, with the highest success rate (98.43%) in predicting desorption reactions.

DIRECT_CLAIMS: The PET architecture scales to 730M parameters (OMat-XL) while maintaining tractable memory usage and computational efficiency due to increased node representation size and unconstrained architecture.
DIRECT_CLAIMS: Conservative PET-OAM models achieve state-of-the-art performance on phonon tasks in matbench-discovery and the best overall accuracy in predicting shear modulus among tested models.
ARTICLE: Pushing the limits of unconstrained machine-learned interatomic potentials

DIRECT_CLAIMS: GAP predicts diamond lattice parameter (3.539 Å) very close to DFT-LDA reference (3.532 Å), outperforming screened Tersoff potential (3.566 Å), with bulk modulus and elastic constants reasonably close to DFT reference values.

DIRECT_CLAIMS: GAP predictions for Young's modulus of amorphous carbon agree very well with experimental values at all relevant densities, while screened Tersoff potential captures the trend but significantly overestimates absolute values.

DIRECT_CLAIMS: DeePMD-kit is an open-source software package that facilitates molecular dynamics simulations using Deep Potential machine learning potentials for computational chemistry and materials science.
DIRECT_CLAIMS: DeePMD-kit supports multiple atomic descriptor types including local frame, DeepPot-SE, attention-based, and hybrid descriptors.
DIRECT_CLAIMS: DeePMD-kit APIs have been integrated into multiple third-party MD packages including LAMMPS, i-PI, GROMACS, AMBER, OpenMM, and ABACUS.
DIRECT_CLAIMS: DeePMD-kit supports interpolation between Deep Potential models and empirical pairwise potentials for cases where DFT calculations fail at close interatomic distances.

NAME: DeepH-E3
TYPE: method
DIRECT_CLAIMS: DeepH-E3 provides a universal E(3)-equivariant deep-learning framework that exactly preserves Euclidean symmetry of the DFT Hamiltonian, including spin-orbit coupling.

DIRECT_CLAIMS: DeepH-E3 predicts DFT Hamiltonian matrix elements with sub‑meV mean absolute error, reducing the error by roughly a factor of two compared with the original DeepH method across diverse material systems.

DIRECT_CLAIMS: DeepH-E3 enables accurate electronic‑structure calculations for supercells larger than 10⁴ atoms, reducing computational cost by several orders of magnitude and allowing calculations in minutes on a single GPU versus months on thousands of CPU cores.

DIRECT_CLAIMS: DeepH‑E3 reproduces the band structure of magic‑angle twisted bilayer graphene (θ = 1.08°, 11 164 atoms) in excellent agreement with DFT and low‑energy continuum models, correctly capturing the flat bands near the Fermi level.
DATASET_METRIC: graphene

NAME: DeepH‑E3
TYPE: cited_work

DIRECT_CLAIMS: DeepH‑E3 reproduces the band structure of magic‑angle twisted bilayer graphene (θ = 1.08°, 11 164 atoms) in excellent agreement with DFT and low‑energy continuum models, correctly capturing the flat bands near the Fermi level.

DIRECT_CLAIMS: DeepH‑E3 predicts a spin‑orbit‑coupling‑induced topological quantum phase transition in twisted bilayer Bi₂Te₃, evidenced by band‑gap closing and reopening and a change of the Z₂ invariant from 0 to 1 as SOC strength increases.
DIRECT_CLAIMS: DeepH‑E3 attains sub‑meV accuracy after training on only a few hundred DFT calculations of small, non‑twisted structures, demonstrating high data efficiency.
DIRECT_CLAIMS: DeepH‑E3 generalizes across diverse material systems—including graphene, MoS₂, bismuthene, Bi₂Se₃, and Bi₂Te₃—achieving consistently sub‑meV Hamiltonian prediction errors.
ARTICLE: Deep-learning electronic-structure calculation of magnetic superstructures

NAME: Gaussian Approximation Potential (GAP) for silicon
TYPE: method

DIRECT_CLAIMS: The Gaussian Approximation Potential (GAP) for silicon reproduces density functional theory reference results across a wide range of observable properties, including bulk crystal, liquid, amorphous phases, and point, line, and plane defects.
DIRECT_CLAIMS: For bulk elastic constants (B, C11, C12, C44) the GAP model achieves fractional errors of less than 10% relative to DFT, outperforming all other evaluated interatomic potentials.

DIRECT_CLAIMS: Surface energies of the (111), (110) and (100) silicon cleavage planes are predicted by GAP with errors of around 2% relative to DFT, which is comparable or better than other potentials.

DIRECT_CLAIMS: Formation energies of vacancy and interstitial point defects (hexagonal, tetrahedral, dumbbell) are predicted by GAP within 10% of DFT values, providing uniform accuracy across these defects.
ARTICLE: Machine learning a general purpose interatomic potential for silicon

DIRECT_CLAIMS: LiFlow achieves speed‑ups of up to ~600,000× over ab initio molecular dynamics (and ~400× over MLIP), predicting a 1 ns trajectory in 48 s for a 2 × 2 × 1 LGPS supercell and 352 s for a 4 × 4 × 4 supercell.
DIRECT_CLAIMS: The computational cost of LiFlow scales linearly with the number of atoms (O(n)), in contrast to the cubic scaling (O(n³)) of ab initio molecular dynamics.

DIRECT_CLAIMS: LiFlow trained on 25 ps ab initio molecular dynamics trajectories can generate stable trajectories up to 1 ns in larger (4 × 4 × 4) supercells, reproducing lithium self‑diffusivity, activation energies, and temperature dependence comparable to long AIMD simulations.
